TREATING THE EMPEROR:
CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES
Robert Doane
EAMP, L.Ac.
Owner of the Acupuncture & Wellness Center, P.S.
www.doane.us

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
• Cardiovascular disease is the number 1 cause of 
death in the United States. 
• In the USA alone it accounts for 630,000 deaths a 
year. That is 1 in every 4 deaths.  In America 
someone has a heart attack every 40 seconds.
• Each minute in the USA someone dies of a heart 
disease related event.

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
• It is not illogical to assume that this disease 
develops over time. 
• It is usually not an acute problem occurring 
suddenly at an early or an advanced age.

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
• Coronary heart disease (CHD) is the most common 
type of heart disease, killing over 370,000 people 
annually.
• Every year about 735,000 Americans have a heart 
attack. 525,000 of these are a first time heart attack, 
and the other 210,000 are subsequent heart attacks. 
• These figures are from the Center For Disease 
Control and Prevention.

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
• Heart Disease Deaths by Race and Ethnicity in 2008
– Native Americans and Alaskan natives:  
18.4%
– Asians or Pacific Islanders
22.2%
– Non-Hispanic Blacks 
23.8%
– Non-Hispanic Whites
23.8%
– All others
11.8%

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
• Heart Disease in Men:
–Heart disease kills 1 in 4 men in America.
– Heart disease is the leading cause of death in men of all ethnic 
backgrounds except Asian Americans or Pacific islander men. 
Heart disease is second to cancer within these two ethnic groups.
– About 8.5% of all white men, 7.9% of black men, and 6.3% of 
Mexican American men have coronary heart disease.
–Between 70% and 89% of sudden cardiac events occur in men.

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
• Heart Disease in Women:
– Heart disease is the leading cause of death for women in the U.S.  
In 2013,  289,758 women lost their lives to heart disease.  
That is approximately 1 in every 4 female deaths.
– Approximately the same number of men and women die of heart 
disease in America.
– Heart disease is the leading cause of death for African American 
and white women.
– Heart disease and cancer kill approximately the same number of 
Hispanic women. 
– Heart disease is second only to cancer with respect to American 
Indian, Alaska Native, and Asian or Pacific Islander women.

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
Almost two-thirds of women who die 
suddenly of coronary heart disease 
have no previous symptoms.

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
• Major warning signs for a heart attack are:
– Chest pain or discomfort
– Upper body pain or discomfort in the arms, 
back, neck, jaw or upper stomach
– Shortness of breath
– Nausea, lightheadedness, or cold sweats

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
• Major risk factors are: high blood pressure, high 
cholesterol, smoking, and excessive stress or shock.
• Other risk factors are: diabetes, obesity, poor diet, 
physical inactivity, and excessive alcohol use.

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
•Heart Disease costs in the United States total 
approximately $200 billion each year.
• This includes the cost of health care services, 
medications, and lost productivity.

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
• In general heart disease describes a range of 
conditions affecting the heart.
• Diseases under the umbrella of heart disease include 
heart failure, (congestive heart failure), heart blood 
vessel diseases, heart rhythm problems, heart 
defects, heart muscle problems, heart valve 
problems, heart pumping problems, etc.
• The term heart disease is used interchangeably with 
the term “cardiovascular disease.”

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
Heart Failure (HF)
Heart failure is often referred to as Congestive Heart Failure (CHF).
- Heart failure occurs when the heart is unable to pump 
sufficiently to maintain blood flow to meet the body’s needs.
- Symptoms include shortness of breath, excessive tiredness, 
and leg swelling (not usually chest pain).
- Common causes are coronary artery disease, previous heart 
attacks, high blood pressure, atrial fibrillation, valvular heart 
disease, excessive alcohol use, infection and cardiomyopathy.

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
Heart Failure (HF)
Two main types of of Heart failure: 
1.  Heart failure due to left ventricular dysfunction 
2.  Heart failure with normal ejection fraction
The severity of the disease is usually graded by the degree of 
problems with exercise.
Heart failure is not the same as myocardial infarction 
(part of the heart muscle dies) or cardiac arrest (blood flow 
stops altogether).

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
Heart Failure (HF) 
1. Heart failure due to reduced ejection fraction. 
This type is also known as heart failure due to left ventricular 
systolic dysfunction or systolic heart failure. This type occurs 
when the ejection fraction is less than 40%.
2.   Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
This type is also known as diastolic heart failure or heart 
failure with normal ejection fraction.  This type of heart failure 
occurs when the heart muscle contracts well but the ventricle 
does not fill with blood well in the relaxation phase.

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
Heart Failure (HF) 
Left-sided heart failure: Failure of the left side of the heart causes 
blood to backup (be congested) into the lungs.  This causes 
respiratory symptoms such as increase rate of breathing, rales, 
pulmonary edema, and cyanosis (low blood oxygen) in severe 
cases.
- Left-sided failure can also involve either the left ventricle or atrium or 
both.
- Valvular heart disease can either be the result or the cause of left-
sided failure. Mitral valve leakage and aortic valve stenosis are often 
involved.

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
Heart Failure(HF) 
Right-sided failure:Right-sided heart failure is often caused by 
pulmonary heart disease (difficulty with pulmonary circulation, either 
due to hypertension or pulmonic stenosis.)
- Backward failure of the right ventricle leads to congestion of 
systemic veins. This generates excess fluid accumulation in the 
body.  This causes swelling under the skin either in the legs and 
ankles or sometimes in the lower back if the patient spends a lot of 
time lying down.
- In severe cases ascites can develop along with liver enlargement.

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
Heart Failure (HF) 
- Medications may cause or worsen the disease.
- This includes NSAIDS, a number of anesthetic 
agents, and a number of cancer medications.

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
Heart Failure (HF) 

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
Cardiovascular Disease
• Conditions involving narrowing or blockage of coronary 
arteries, large or small.
• Chest pain or angina 
• Stroke
• Conditions affecting the functioning of the heart such as: heart 
muscle weakness or enlargement, valve issues, or rhythm 
problems.

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
• Symptoms of heart disease of the blood vessels 
are:
– Chest pain, chest tightness, chest pressure and 
chest discomfort (angina)
– Shortness of breath
– Pain, numbness weakness or coldness in your 
legs or arms if the blood vessels in those areas 
are narrowed
– Pain in the neck, jaw, throat, upper abdomen or 
upper back

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
• Heart disease symptoms caused by abnormal 
heartbeats (heart arrhythmias)
– Fluttering in your chest
– Racing heartbeat
– Slow heartbeat
– Chest pain or discomfort
– Shortness of breath
– Lightheadedness
– Dizziness
–
Fainting (syncope) or near fainting

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
• Heart disease symptoms caused by heart 
defects
– Pale gray or blue skin color (cyanosis)
– Swelling in the legs, abdomen or areas around the eyes
– In an infant, shortness of breath during feedings, leading to 
poor weight gain
– Easily getting short of breath during exercise or activity
– Easily tiring during exercise or activity
– Swelling in the hands, ankles or feet

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
• Heart disease symptoms caused by heart 
infections.  
• Endocarditis is an infection that affects the inner membrane 
that separates the chambers and valves of the heart 
(endocardium).
– Fever
– Shortness of breath, weakness or fatigue
– Swelling in your legs or abdomen
– Changes in your heart rhythm
– Dry or persistent cough
– Skin rashes or unusual spots

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
• Heart disease symptoms caused by valvular 
heart disease
The heart has 4 valves
- the aortic, mitral, pulmonary and tricuspid valves -
that open and close to direct blood flow through your 
heart.  Valves may be damaged by a variety of 
conditions leading to narrowing (stenosis), leaking 
(regurgitation or insufficiency) or improper closing 
(prolapse).

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
FLOW OF BLOOD THROUGH THE HEART
• The right side of the heart, comprising the right atrium and 
ventricle, collects and pumps blood to the lungs through the 
pulmonary arteries.
• The lungs refresh the blood with a new supply of oxygen.           
The lungs also breathe out carbon dioxide, a waste product.
• Oxygen-rich blood then enters the left side of the heart, 
comprising of the left atrium and ventricle.
• The left side of the heart pumps blood through the aorta to 
supply tissues throughout the body with oxygen (Qi) and 
nutrients (Ying Qi).

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
Heart valves
-
Four valves within the heart keep the blood moving the right 
way by opening only one way and only when they need to. To 
function properly, the valve must be formed properly, must open 
all the way and must close tightly so there is no leakage. 
The four valves are:
Tricuspid
Mitral
Pulmonary
Aortic

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
Diagram of blood flow 
through the chambers
and valves of the heart

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
Heart Beats
- A beating heart contracts and relaxes in a continuous 
cycle. During contraction (systole), your ventricles 
contract, forcing blood into the vessels to your lungs and 
body.
- During relaxation (diastole), the ventricles are filled with 
blood coming from the upper chambers (left and right 
atria) which are themselves contracting.

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
Heart’s Electrical System
- The heart’s electrical wiring keeps it beating, which controls 
the continuous exchange of oxygen-rich blood with oxygen-
poor blood.
- This exchange keeps you alive. Electrical impulses begin high 
in the right atrium and travel through specialized pathways to 
the ventricles, delivering the signal for the heart to pump.
- The conduction system keeps your heart beating in a 
coordinated and normal rhythm, which keeps blood 
circulating.

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
Causes of Heart Disease
- Cardiovascular disease usually refers to heart or 
blood vessel problems. The most common cause 
of cardiovascular disease is atherosclerosis which 
is a buildup of fatty plaques in your arteries. 

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
Development of Atherosclerosis
- Atherosclerosis is a process in which blood and fats, 
such as cholesterol and other substances, build up 
on the artery walls. Eventually, deposits called 
plaques may form. The deposits may narrow—or 
block—the arteries.  These plaques can also 
rupture, causing a blood clot..

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
Development of Atherosclerosis
.

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
Causes of Heart Arrhythmias
- Congenital heart defects
- Coronary artery disease
- High blood pressure 
- Diabetes
- Smoking
- Excessive use of alcohol or caffeine
- Drug abuse 
- Stress
- Medications
- Valvular heart disease

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
Causes of Heart Arrhythmias
- In a healthy person with a normal, healthy heart,     
it’s unlikely for a fatal arrhythmia to develop without 
some outside trigger, such as an electrical shock or 
the use of illegal drugs.  That’s primarily because a 
healthy person’s heart is free from any abnormal 
conditions that cause an arrhythmia, such as an 
area of scarred tissue.

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
Causes of Heart Arrhythmias
- In a heart that’s diseased or deformed, the heart’s 
electrical impulses may not properly start or travel 
through the heart, making arrhythmias more likely to 
develop.

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
Causes of Congenital Heart Defects
- Congenital heart defects usually develop while a baby is in the 
womb.  Heart defects can develop as the heart develops, 
about a month after conception, changing the flow of blood in 
the heart. 
- Some medical conditions, medications and genes may play a 
role in causing heart defects.
- Heart defects can also develop in adults. As you age, the 
heart’s structure can change, causing a heart defect.

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
Causes of Congenital Heart Defects
- Heart defects can also develop in adults.      
As we age, our heart’s structure can change, 
causing a heart defect.

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
Cardiomyopathy
- Cardiomyopathy is a group of diseases that affect the heart 
muscle. Early on there may be few or no symptoms.  Some 
people may have shortness of breath, feel tired, or have 
swelling of the legs due to heart failure.  An irregular heartbeat 
may occur as well as fainting. 
-Types of cardiomyopathy include:
hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, dilated cardiomyopathy, 
restrictive cardiomyopathy, and takotsubo cardiomyopathy.

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
Types of Cardiomyopathy: Hypertrophic
-  Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy causes the heart muscle to enlarge and 
thicken, usually the left ventricle.
-  Symptoms vary from none to feeling tired, leg swelling, shortness of breath, 
chest pain and fainting.
-  Complications include congestive heart failure, an irregular heartbeat,       
and sudden cardiac death. 
-  Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is usually caused by genetics or reaction to 
drugs, specifically an immunosuppressant drug called Tacrolimus (Prograf, 
Advagraf, Protopic). It is the most common type of cardiomyopathy. 1 in 500 
people are affected, with a 1% a year chance of death.

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019
Doane.us
Doane Seminars
TREATING THE EMPEROR
Types of Cardiomyopathy: Dilated
-  Dilated cardiomyopathy is a condition in which the heart becomes enlarged 
and cannot pump blood effectively. The ventricles enlarge and weaken.
-  Symptoms vary from none to feeling tired, leg swelling, shortness of breath, 
chest pain and fainting.
-  Complications include heart failure, heart valve disease, or an irregular 
heartbeat.
-  Causes include genetics, alcohol, cocaine, certain toxins, certain infections, 
coronary artery disease and high blood pressure. 1 in 2500 people are 
affected. The 5 year survival rate is 50%.

All Rights Reserved. Copyright Lucky Falcon LLC d/b/a Doane Online Education 2019

Types of Cardiomyopathy: Restrictive
- Restrictive cardiomyopathy is a form of cardiomyopathy in which the 
walls of the heart are rigid (usually the ventricle), but not thickened.

protein, known as amyloid fibrils, build up in tissue.
- When the disease affects the heart it can cause both diastolic and 
systolic heart failure.

Heart Infection
-
A heart infection, such as pericarditis, endocarditis or myocarditis, is caused when an 
irritant, such as bacteria, viruses or chemicals, reach the heart muscle. It can also be 
triggered by an autoimmune inflammatory condition. In all the above cases this 
condition can lead to heart failure.
-
Endocarditis is an inflammation of the inner layer of the heart, the endocardium. It 
usually involves the heart valves.
-
Myocarditis is an inflammation of the middle layer of the heart wall; the heart muscle. 
Heart muscle differs from skeletal muscle by its ability to contract rhythmically. 
-
Pericarditis is an inflammation of the fibroserous sac enclosing the heart. 
-
The most common causes of heart infection include:
-
Bacteria
-
Viruses-usually acute
-
Parasites
-
Fungi or tuberculosis (chronic)

-Sick Sinus Syndrome (SSS):
SSS is not a disease, but a group of signs or symptoms that show

-Ventricular Fibrillation (VF):
Sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) caused by ventricular fibrillation is the 
cause of half of all heart related deaths. In VF, the heartbeat is fast 
and chaotic, causing the lower heart chambers to spasm.

Diagnosing Heart Failure
Chest X-ray:  X-ray images help to see the condition of the heart and lungs. In heart 
failure the heart can appear enlarged and fluid build up can be visible in the lungs.
Electrocardiogram (ECG):  This records your heart’s electrical activity It helps 
diagnose heart rhythm problems (bundle branch block) or damage to the heart from a 
heart attack.
Echocardiogram:  This test uses sound waves to produce a video image of the 
functioning of the heart. The percentage of blood pumped out of the left ventricle is 
shown (ejection fraction). It also shows any valve dysfunction. It helps distinguish 
systolic heart failure from diastolic failure. With systolic failure the ejection fraction will 
be 40 percent or lower. With diastolic failure the EJ remains normal (55 to 70 
percent).
Coronary catheterization:  In this test, a thin, flexible tube (catheter) is inserted into 
a blood vessel and guided into the coronary arteries. A dye injected through the 
catheter makes the arteries supplying blood to the heart visible on an x-ray. This test 
helps to identify coronary occlusions. The procedure also allows the doctor to take a 
biopsy of the heart wall if needed.

Diagnosing Heart Failure
Nuclear stress test: This test shows how well the heart works during physical 
activity. A radioactive substance is injected in a vein. You wait for 30 minutes and with 
a special camera you can see how well the substance has traveled through the blood 
and into the heart. The patient then walks on a treadmill or uses a stationary bike. The 
blood pressure and heart rhythm are monitored with an ECG. As the patient increases 
their activity any coronary blockage tends to reveal itself. This test is 91% effective 
over a standard treadmill test which is approximately 65% effective.
Coronary calcium scan: This CT scan can detect and measure the amount of 
calcium in the walls of the coronary arteries. Build up of calcium is a sign of 
arteriosclerosis/atherosclerosis. The higher the score the more likely the patient will 
have coronary heart disease.
Blood tests: There are blood tests for specific markers indicative of heart failure, 
such as hormone called brain natriuretic peptide (BNP). BNP is secreted at high 
levels by the heart when the heart is overworked. The BNP blood test may help detect 
and diagnose heart failure in its early stages. Ultrasensitive C-Reactive protein is 
another marker indicating atherosclerosis. A new test for Lp-PLA2 is also available. 
This marker is also indicative of advanced coronary artery inflammation.

FATIGUE: Medical Definition 
  
Fatigue is defined as a subjective felling of tiredness which is distinct 
from weakness, and has a gradual onset.  Fatigue can be alleviated by 
periods of rest. 
 
Medically, fatigue is a non-specific symptom, which means that it has 
many possible causes.  Fatigue is considered a symptom, rather than a 
sign, because it is a subjective feeling reported by the patient, rather 
than an objective one that can be observed by others. 
 
FATIGUE 
• There are two types of fatigue: 
• PHYSICAL FATGUE 
• MENTAL FATUGUE

FATIGUE 
PHYSICAL FATIGUE 
     Physical fatigue is the temporary physical inability of a muscle to       
 perform optimally. 
 
   CAUSES:   
• Lack of energy in the muscle 
• Decrease in efficiency of neuromuscular junction 
• Reduction of the drive originating from the central nervous system 
FATIGUE 
MENTAL FATIGUE 
 Temporary inability to maintain optimal cognitive performance 
CAUSES: 
• The perception of mental fatigue is commonly believed to be modulated 
by the brain’s reticular activating systems (RAS) 
• Can manifest as somnolence, lethargy or Directed Attention Fatigue 
FATIGUE 
 
Fatigue differs from sleepiness in that it is 
considered a more long-term or chronic 
condition than somnolence.

• PROLONGED FATIGUE: 
Is a persistent fatigue lasting at least one month 
 
• CHRONIC FATIGUE:

ANXIETY: Medical Definition 
 
Anxiety is an emotional experience characterized by an unpleasant state 
of inner turmoil. It is sometimes defined as the feeling one gets when 
facing an unpleasant situation with insufficient coping skills. 
 
 
Symptoms may include feelings of dread over upcoming events, fear, 
worry, uneasiness, irritability, and fatigue. 
 
Indicators include, but are not limited to, restlessness, lack of 
concentration, sleeplessness, and muscle tension.

ANXIETY VS. FEAR  
Fear: an appropriate reaction to 
a currently perceived threat, often 
involving a physiological fight-or-
flight response.  
Anxiety: the feeling of dread 
over anticipated unpleasantness in 
the future. 
ANXIETY 
 
 
Anxiety is considered to be a normal occurrence if experienced by 
situation or temporarily. 
 
If anxiety is experienced regularly and/or on a consistent basis, then the 
patient may suffer from an anxiety disorder. 
 
COMMON ANXIETY DISORDERS 
TYPES OF DISORDERS: 
• Existential Anxiety:  
–  The basic human condition of lack of control

disorder due to a general medical condition;

substance-induced mood disorder.

CHRONIC STRESS

CHRONIC STRESS 
PHYSIOLOGICAL RESPONSES: 
 
The endocrine system releases epinephrine, causing the blood vessels 
to contract and the heart rate to increase. 
 
Cortisol is also released, which causes the glucose levels in the blood to 
rise. This is designed to give the body more energy during times of 
duress. 
 
Unfortunately, when one experiences chronic stress this chemical 
activity is going on continuously, causing enormous wear and tear on the 
body.

ACUPUNCTUE FOR FATIGUE 
 
The most important concept to remember with acupuncture is whether 
you wish to create a sympathetic (excitatory) response or a 
parasympathetic (relaxing) response in the patient. 
 
Patients with fatigue due to deficiency need to be stimulated. 
Therefore, do not leave the needles in for more than nine minutes. 
ACUPUNCTURE FOR FATIGUE

• ST 36, GB 34 
• LI 4, SJ 5

CHINESE MEDICINE AND ANXIETY 
Anxiety is usually a problem with the heart, liver, kidney, or all three. 
 
In most cases, the heart pulse is weak and the liver pulse is too high and 
too wiry and strong. 
 
Consequently, the heart has to be strengthened and the liver has to be 
calmed down. 
 
Anxiety can come from a deep liver pulse but this is more associated 
with depression and frustration.

CHINESE MEDICINE AND DEPRESSION 
 
 
Depression in Chinese medicine can also be 
divided into excess and deficient types. 
 
CHINESE MEDICINE AND DEPRESSION 
Deficiency:  
 weakness in the lung, heart and kidney 
 
Excess:  
 stagnation with or without heat in the 
 liver and gall bladder and congestive 
 heart problems. 
DEFICIENCY CAUSING DEPRESSION 
Depression can easily arise if the patient 
feels a lack of vitality. 
 
The herbal and pulse presentations for 
fatigue in this webinar will cure depression 
caused by deficiency.

1.	Ensure	proper	palpation	of	the	5	Cun	position-related	pulses	(Cun	Pulse,	Yin	Wei	Pulse,	Yang	Wei	Pulse,	Large	
Vessel	Pulse	and	Mitral	Valve	Pulse).	
2.	Upon	analysing	the	Cun	Pulse,	rotate	the	diagnostic	hand's	index	finger	pad	30-40	degrees	distally,	toward	the	
scaphoid	bone.	Do	not	rotate	the	diagnostic	fingers	for	the	Styloid,	Guan,	Chi	and	Proximal	Pulses.	
3.	The	Large	Vessel	pulse	is	precisely	located	at	the	wrist	crease	junction	of	the	superficial	palmar	arch,	the	flexor	
carpi	radialis	tendon,	and	the	scaphoid	bone.	Compressed	pen-tip	pulses	palpated	distal	or	medial	to	this	junction	
are	not	considered	the	Large	Vessel	pulse.	
4.	Do	not	confuse	the	Yin	Wei	Pulse	or	Yang	Wei	Pulse	for	the	Cun	Pulse.	Palpate	the	Cun	Pulse	with	the	rotated	
finger	pad	in	the	central	region	of	the	Cun	"Valley."	Palpate	the	other	pulses	with	the	finger	pad	at	the	
perpendicular	angle.	
5.	Properly	"gap"	the	radial	styloid	process	to	locate	the	Cun	and	Guan	positions.		With	palpating	the	Guan	
position,	ensure	that	the	diagnostic	finger	pad	is	not	on	the	Proximal	Radial	Styloid	pulse.	
6.	Following	the	proper	"gapping"	of	the	radial	styloid	process,	use	the	"Ruler	technique"	to	correctly	identify	the	
Chi	position.		The	Proximal	Pulses	are	located	immediately	proximal	to	the	Chi	position	and	can	extend	several	
finger	lengths	in	the	proximal	direction.	
7.	Improper	positioning	of	the	finger	pads	too	medially,	adjacent	to	the	flexor	carpi	radialis	tendon,	compromises	
correct	pulse	diagnosis.	
8.	Palpate	the	pulses	predominantly	using	the	diagnostic	hand's	index	finger	pad.		Include	the	other	finger	pads	in	
the	palpation	of	the	Proximal	Pulses	or	testing	for	particular	pulse	presentations	to	be	described	in	future	MPD®	
texts.		Do	not	palpate	the	pulses	with	an	excessive	pressure	that	occludes	the	radial	artery.

Five Levels of Pulse Depth
First,	identify	the	skin	level	by	placing	the	diagnostic	hand	finger	pads	
on	the	skin	without	applying	pressure.		
Second,	identify	the	bone	level	by	applying	substantial	pressure	to	the	
pulse	until	you	touch	the	bone.		
Third,	locate	the	middle	level	in	between	the	skin	and	bone	levels.		
The	 proper	 identification	 of	 these	 three	 levels	 provides	 a	 reference	
point	for	the	location	of	all	five	depth	levels.	

All	Rights	Reserved.	Copyright	Lucky	Falcon	LLC	d/b/a	Doane	Online	Educa?on	2021	
Five Levels of Pulse Depth
Skin	Level:	Palpate	the	skin	level	by	placing	the	diagnostic	hand's	finger	pads	on	the	
skin	above	the	pulse	positions.	No	pressure	is	applied	to	perceive	the	pulse	at	this	level.	
The	skin	level	is	a	pathological	pulse	depth	that	invariably	represents	dysfunction	of	the	
corresponding	organ	systems/anatomical	regions	of	the	pulse	positions.			
Superficial	Level:	Palpate	the	superficial	level	with	gentle	pressure	just	below	the	skin	
level.	This	depth	is	the	proper	physiological	depth	of	both	the	right	and	left	Cun	
positions.		
Middle	Level:	Palpate	the	middle	level	with	gentle	pressure	below	the	superficial	level.	
This	depth	is	the	proper	physiological	depth	of	both	the	right	and	left	Guan	positions.		
Deep	Level:	Palpate	the	deep	level	with	gentle	pressure	below	the	middle	level.	This	
depth	is	the	proper	physiological	depth	of	both	the	right	and	left	Chi	positions.		
Bone	Level:	Palpate	the	bone	level	with	sufficient	pressure	to	touch	the	radial	bone.	
regions	of	the	pulse	positions.

Pathological Pulse Force
-	The	resistance	level	of	the	pulse	to	pressure	determines	the	pulse	force.		
-	The	healthy	pulses,	in	the	proper	"home,"	preserve	a	balanced	level	of	
resistance	to	palpation,	neither	too	much	or	too	little.		
-	Forceful	pulses	maintain	STRONG	resistance	to	pressure.		The	forceful	
nature	reflects	a	pathological	EXCESS	condition	of	either	Heat	or	Cold.	
-	Forceless	pulses	fail	to	resist	pressure	and	"give	way"	with	no	perceivable	
pulse	underneath.	The	forceless	nature	reflects	a	pathological	DEFICIENT	
condition	of	either	Qi	Deficiency,	Yang	deficiency,	Blood	Deficiency,	Yin	
Deficiency,	Yin	deficiency	with	Increased	Heat	or	a	combination	thereof.

Up-Down Pulse
-	The	diagnostic	fingers	sharply	elevate	
during	the	ascending	phase	of	the	pulse	
wave	and	then	collapse	in	the	descending	
phase.	This	creates	a	mechanical	up-down	
sensation	along	the	radial	artery.		
-	This	quality	can	result	from	an	aortic	
valve	regurgitation,	generally	due	to	aortic	
valve	insufficiency	and	aortic	stenosis,	
most	common	in	patients	of	senior	age.	

All	Rights	Reserved.	Copyright	Lucky	Falcon	LLC	d/b/a	Doane	Online	Educa?on	2021	
Viscous Blood Pulse
-	The	viscous-blood	pulse	indicates	a	higher	
density	of	particles	in	the	bloodstream.	This	
issue	can	result	from	high	blood	lipids	and	
glucose	from	poor	diet,	accumulated	toxins/
waste	products,	and	blood	disorders	in	which	
abnormal	blood	cell	production	is	involved.		
-	In	this	case,	the	vessel	boundaries	are	clearly	
palpable,	but	the	fluid	within	the	artery	feels	
thick,	viscous	and	sluggish.

What is Medical Pulse Diagnosis
®
?
‐ MPD® is a tried and true SYSTEMATIC method that is the result of twenty years 
of high‐volume clinical experience. The unique discoveries and cardiovascular 
emphasis of this method come from continually observing the same pulse signs 
and concurrent symptoms in thousands of patients. Modern medical research 
continues to support the clinical observations of MPD® .
‐ The MPD® pulse positions differ from most traditional pulse teachings and 
provide an advanced standardization of pulse locations for accurate diagnosis.
‐ The comprehensive pulse analysis informs the practitioner of the multiple 
pathological conditions influencing each patient’s disease expression. This 
comprehensive diagnosis guides the most effective MPD® treatment strategies.
‐ It is clear that the majority of Chinese medicine practitioners 
lack confidence in their ability to correctly diagnose and treat 
patient illness in the clinical setting. 
‐ For most, this is not due to a lack of intelligence or 
motivation, but rather an educational approach that 
insufficiently develops the diagnostic skills necessary to 
navigate complex patient cases. 
‐ With dedicated learning, Medical Pulse Diagnosis®(MPD®) 
will rapidly guide your success in the practice of Chinese 
Medicine.

Avoiding Common Beginner Mistakes
1.Ensure proper palpation of the 5 Cun position‐related pulses (Cun Pulse, Yin Wei Pulse, Yang Wei Pulse, Large 
Vessel Pulse and Mitral Valve Pulse).
2.Upon analyzing the Cun Pulse, rotate the diagnostic hand's index finger pad 30‐40 degrees distally, toward 
the scaphoid bone. Do not rotate the diagnostic fingers for the Styloid, Guan, Chi and Proximal Pulses.
3.The Large Vessel pulse is precisely located at the wrist crease junction of the superficial palmar arch, the 
flexor carpi radialis tendon, and the scaphoid bone. Compressed pen‐tip pulses palpated distal or medial to this 
junction are not considered the Large Vessel pulse.
4.Do not confuse the Yin Wei Pulse or Yang Wei Pulse for the Cun Pulse. Palpate the Cun Pulse with the rotated 
finger pad in the central region of the Cun "Valley." Palpate the other pulses with the finger pad at the 
perpendicular angle.
5. Properly "gap" the radial styloid process to locate the Cun and Guan positions.  With palpating the Guan 
position, ensure that the diagnostic finger pad is not on the Proximal Radial Styloid pulse.
6.Following the proper "gapping" of the radial styloid process, use the "Ruler technique" to correctly identify 
the Chi position.  The Proximal Pulses are located immediately proximal to the Chi position and can extend 
several finger lengths in the proximal direction.
7.Improper positioning of the finger pads too medially, adjacent to the flexor carpi radialis tendon, 
compromises correct pulse diagnosis.
8.Palpate the pulses predominantly using the diagnostic hand's index finger pad.  Include the other finger pads 
in the palpation of the Proximal Pulses or testing for particular pulse presentations to be described in future

What is Medical Pulse Diagnosis
®
?
-MPD® is a tried and true SYSTEMATIC method that is the result of twenty years 
of high-volume clinical experience. The unique discoveries and cardiovascular 
emphasis of this method come from continually observing the same pulse signs 
and concurrent symptoms in thousands of patients. Modern medical research 
continues to support the clinical observations of MPD® .
-The MPD® pulse positions differ from most traditional pulse teachings and 
provide an advanced standardization of pulse locations for accurate diagnosis.
-The comprehensive pulse analysis informs the practitioner of the multiple 
pathological conditions influencing each patient’s disease expression.This 
comprehensive diagnosis guides the most effective MPD® treatment strategies.

Avoiding Common Beginner Mistakes
1.Ensure proper palpation of the 5 Cun position-related pulses (Cun Pulse, Yin Wei Pulse, Yang Wei Pulse, Large 
Vessel Pulse and Mitral Valve Pulse).
2.Upon analyzing the Cun Pulse, rotate the diagnostic hand's index finger pad 30-40 degrees distally, toward 
the scaphoid bone. Do not rotate the diagnostic fingers for the Styloid, Guan, Chi and Proximal Pulses.
3.The Large Vessel pulse is precisely located at the wrist crease junction of the superficial palmar arch, the 
flexor carpi radialis tendon, and the scaphoid bone. Compressed pen-tip pulses palpated distal or medial to this 
junction are not considered the Large Vessel pulse.
4.Do not confuse the Yin Wei Pulse or Yang Wei Pulse for the Cun Pulse. Palpate the Cun Pulse with the rotated 
finger pad in the central region of the Cun "Valley." Palpate the other pulses with the finger pad at the 
perpendicular angle.
5. Properly "gap" the radial styloid process to locate the Cun and Guan positions.  With palpating the Guan 
position, ensure that the diagnostic finger pad is not on the Proximal Radial Styloid pulse.
6.Following the proper "gapping" of the radial styloid process, use the "Ruler technique" to correctly identify 
the Chi position.  The Proximal Pulses are located immediately proximal to the Chi position and can extend 
several finger lengths in the proximal direction.
7.Improper positioning of the finger pads too medially, adjacent to the flexor carpi radialis tendon, 
compromises correct pulse diagnosis.
8.Palpate the pulses predominantly using the diagnostic hand's index finger pad.  Include the other finger pads 
in the palpation of the Proximal Pulses or testing for particular pulse presentations to be described in future 
MPD® texts.  Do not palpate the pulses with an excessive pressure that occludes the radial artery.

Pathological Pulse Force
- The resistance level of the pulse to pressure determines the pulse force. 
- The healthy pulses, in the proper "home," preserve a balanced level of 
resistance to palpation, neither too much or too little. 
-Forceful pulses maintain STRONG resistance to pressure. The forceful 
nature reflects a pathological EXCESS condition of either Heat or Cold.
-Forceless pulses fail to resist pressure and "give way" with no 
perceivable pulse underneath.The forceless nature reflects a pathological 
DEFICIENT condition of either Qi Deficiency, Yang deficiency, Blood 
Deficiency, Yin Deficiency, Yin deficiency with Increased Heat or a 
combination thereof.

Pathological Pulse Width
- The healthy width (thick or thin) quality of the pulse is relative to the 
physical size and constitution of each patient. 
- Pulses that are too thick are the result of either Excess Heat, Excess 
Fire or Qi Deficiency.  
- Thin pulses that maintain resistance to pressure are due to Excess Cold 
or Severe Blood Stasis with Excess Cold. 
- Thin pulses that "give way" with pressure are due to Yang Deficiency, 
Blood Deficiency or Yin Deficiency.

Up-Down Pulse
- The diagnostic fingers sharply elevate 
during the ascending phase of the pulse 
wave and then collapse in the descending 
phase. This creates a mechanical up-down 
sensation along the radial artery. 
- This quality can result from an aortic 
valve regurgitation, generally due to 
aortic valve insufficiency and aortic 
stenosis, most common in patients of 
senior age.

Doane Seminars
Viscous Blood Pulse
- The viscous-blood pulse indicates a higher 
density of particles in the bloodstream. This 
issue can result from high blood lipids and 
glucose from poor diet, accumulated 
toxins/waste products, and blood disorders in 
which abnormal blood cell production is 
involved. 
- In this case, the vessel boundaries are 
clearly palpable, but the fluid within the 
artery feels thick, viscous and sluggish.

Stiff Pulse
- The stiff pulse represents the hardening of 
the arterial vessel system.  With this pulse, the 
entire radial artery is palpable as a hard, 
slightly thick, wiry pulse that is resistant to 
pressure. 
- This compromised vessel structure limits 
optimal blood circulation to both internal and 
external regions of the body and may provoke 
a myriad of health conditions.

systemic narrowing of the inside diameter of 
the arterial walls due to inflammation and 
cell proliferation.

feels slightly thick and swollen. Increased 
palpatory pressure also demonstrates a 
spongy quality of the vessel wall.

Why does this work?  Eating in this manner makes every meal force the body to burn fat. 
Each meal forces the pancreas to produce Glucagon which is the command hormone that 
tells the body to burn fat. We have taken away any food which will force the pancreas to 
produce insulin. Insulin is the command hormone that tells the body to manufacture fat.  
 
Buy eating meals which do not break down into sugar immediately the patient’s pancreas 
has a chance to repair itself by not being forced to release insulin, which it is struggling to 
do because of the Diabetes. Blood sugars rapidly come down and the patient quickly finds 
themselves overmedicated. Blood sugar levels fall into the 80’s and their doctor has to 
reduce the medication to avoid exhaustion. 
 
The result is an A1c that quickly drops below 6 and normalized blood sugar levels without 
medication. Do they still have Diabetes? Theoretically, but in practice, no. In addition the 
patient will loose 30 pounds in 5 months. Blood pressure is usually normalized. Blood 
sugars are normalized and the patient can loose as much weight as desired.

• High blood pressure has no known cause in Western 
Medicine. For almost all Hypertensive patients 
Western Medicine is completely at a loss to tell us 
why. They just say it is a multitude of causes.  
• High blood pressure is the force in your blood vessels 
when your heart beats and when you heart rests. 
High blood pressure makes the heart work harder to 
pump blood through the body and causes damage to 
the blood vessels. It also causes the walls of the 
heart to thicken which enlarges the heart.

• The impulse that results from left ventricular ejection 
can be transmitted down the aorta at a velocity 20 
times greater than the velocity of the ejected blood 
bolus. The peak of this arterial pulse is the systolic 
blood pressure. (Mayo Clinic) 
• The size of the arterial pulse is affected by the left 
ventricular ejection volume and the rate of ejection 
along with the elastic properties of the vessels 
themselves.

• If the radial pulse is absent it could be due a blockage 
such as a thrombi or claudication. 
• If the radial pulse is weak (low volume) with a low 
amplitude it is referred to as a hypokinetic pulse. This 
usually means cardiac output is low due to a low ejection 
fraction or a narrowing of the aortic valve. 
• Large amplitude pulses in Western Medicine are said to 
be caused by anxiety, fevers, hyperthyroidism, anemia, or 
over-exercising. They can also be caused by a leaking 
aortic valve. These pulses are called hyperkinetic.

ventricle is felt at the radial artery at the wrist almost

beats of the heart.

Pulse Pressure is defined as the difference between the 
difference between the systolic and diastolic pressure. The 
wider the number the greater the risk of heart disease. 
 
A meta-analysis in 2000, which combined the results of 
several studies of 8,000 elderly patients in all, found that a 
10mmHg increase in pulse pressure increased the risk of 
major cardiovascular complications and mortality by almost 
20%. Heightened pressure also increases the risk of A-fib. 
(Blacher et al., 2000)

Normal blood pressure according to the AHA  is 
considered to be a systolic pressure below 120 and a 
Diastolic pressure below 80. 
 
Prehypertension is defined as a systolic pressure 
between 120 to 139 or a Diastolic pressure between 80 
and 89.

Stage 1 high blood pressure is defined as a systolic 
pressure between 140 to 159 and a diastolic between 90 to 
99. 
State 2 high blood pressure is a systolic of 160 or higher and 
a diastolic of 100 or over. 
Hypertension crisis (emergency care needed) is a systolic 
pressure higher than 180 or a diastolic higher than 110. 
If you are an adult and over 60 the treatment goal is a 
systolic pressure of 150 or less and a diastolic of 90 or less.
